From 237aab549676288d9255bb8dcc284738e56eaa31 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Ville=20Syrj=C3=A4l=C3=A4?= <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:54:14 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/vrr: Configure VRR timings after enabling
 TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Apparently ICL may hang with an MCE if we write TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE
before enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL.

Personally I was only able to reproduce a hang (on an Dell XPS 7390
2-in-1) with an external display connected via a dock using a dodgy
type-C cable that made the link training fail. After the failed
link training the machine would hang. TGL seemed immune to the
problem for whatever reason.

BSpec does tell us to configure VRR after enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL
as well. The DMC firmware also does the VRR restore in two stages:
- first stage seems to be unconditional and includes TRANS_VRR_CTL
  and a few other VRR registers, among other things
- second stage is conditional on the DDI being enabled,
  and includes TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL and TRANS_VRR_VMAX/VMIN/FLIPLINE,
  among other things

So let's reorder the steps to match to avoid the hang, and
toss in an extra WARN to make sure we don't screw this up later.

BSpec: 22243
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Ankit Nautiyal <ankit.k.nautiyal@intel.com>
Reported-by: Benjamin Tissoires <bentiss@kernel.org>
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/i915/kernel/-/issues/15777
Tested-by: Benjamin Tissoires <bentiss@kernel.org>
Fixes: dda7dcd9da73 ("drm/i915/vrr: Use fixed timings for platforms that support VRR")
Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260303095414.4331-1-ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com
Reviewed-by: Ankit Nautiyal <ankit.k.nautiyal@intel.com>
(cherry picked from commit 93f3a267c3dd4d811b224bb9e179a10d81456a74)
Signed-off-by: Tvrtko Ursulin <tursulin@ursulin.net>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_vrr.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_vrr.c
index db74744ddb31..bea005752327 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_vrr.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_vrr.c
@@ -597,6 +597,18 @@ void intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(const struct intel_crtc_state *crtc_state)
 	if (!HAS_VRR(display))
 		return;
 
+	/*
+	 * Bspec says:
+	 * "(note: VRR needs to be programmed after
+	 *  TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL and before TRANS_CONF)."
+	 *
+	 * In practice it turns out that ICL can hang if
+	 * TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE are written before
+	 * enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL.
+	 */
+	drm_WARN_ON(display->drm,
+		    !(intel_de_read(display, TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL(display, cpu_transcoder)) & TRANS_DDI_FUNC_ENABLE));
+
 	/*
 	 * This bit seems to have two meanings depending on the platform:
 	 * TGL: generate VRR "safe window" for DSB vblank waits
@@ -939,6 +951,8 @@ void intel_vrr_transcoder_enable(const struct intel_crtc_state *crtc_state)
 {
 	struct intel_display *display = to_intel_display(crtc_state);
 
+	intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);
+
 	if (!intel_vrr_possible(crtc_state))
 		return;
 
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display.c
index 3b8ba8ab76a1..c4246481fc2f 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display.c
@@ -1614,7 +1614,6 @@ static void hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder(const struct intel_crtc_state *crtc_sta
 	}
 
 	intel_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);
-	intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);
 
 	if (cpu_transcoder != TRANSCODER_EDP)
 		intel_de_write(display, TRANS_MULT(display, cpu_transcoder),

The patch fixes a hardware hang on ICL (and potentially other platforms) caused by writing VRR timing registers (`TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE`) before the DDI function is enabled. It reorders the VRR timing configuration to occur after `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` is enabled.

**Modifications in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_vrr.c`:**
- Added a `drm_WARN_ON` check in `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()` to ensure `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` has the `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_ENABLE` bit set when called.
- Moved the call to `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()` from `intel_vrr_transcoder_enable()` (which is invoked after DDI enable) into the same function, ensuring VRR timings are programmed only after the DDI is enabled.

**Modification in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display.c`:**
- Removed the call to `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()` from `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder()`, which was executed before `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` was enabled.

**Relationship:** The change moves the VRR timing setup from a point where the DDI may not yet be active (causing hangs) to a later point where it is guaranteed to be enabled, aligning with the BSpec requirement and the hardware’s ordering constraints.

The relationship between the modifications is a direct relocation: the VRR timing configuration is moved from an early stage (before DDI enable) to a later stage (after DDI enable), aligning with hardware requirements (BSpec 22243) and preventing the reported ICL MCE hang.

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_vrr.c`

1. **Added a WARN check** in `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()` to verify that `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` is already enabled (i.e., `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_ENABLE` bit set) before programming `TRANS_VRR_VMAX`/`FLIPLINE`. This is a safety measure to enforce the correct ordering required by hardware.

2. **Moved the call** to `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()` from the end of `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder()` (in `intel_display.c`) into `intel_vrr_transcoder_enable()`, right at the beginning before the existing VRR enable logic. This ensures the VRR timing registers are programmed after `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` is enabled, preventing a potential hang on ICL.

### Modification in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display.c`

- **Removed the call** to `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()` from `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder()`. This call was originally placed after `intel_set_transcoder_timings()`, but before enabling `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` (since `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` is enabled later in the transcoder enable sequence). Moving it to `intel_vrr_transcoder_enable()` aligns the order with hardware requirements.

### Relationship Between Changes

The two modifications are directly linked: the call was moved from one file/function to another, and a guard (WARN) was added to the moved function to enforce the new ordering. The core fix is the reordering: VRR timing registers (`TRANS_VRR_VMAX`, `TRANS_VRR_FLIPLINE`) must be written **after** `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` is enabled, not before. This prevents a hang on ICL (and is consistent with BSpec guidance). The removal from `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder()` ensures the call no longer happens at the old incorrect point, while the addition to `intel_vrr_transcoder_enable()` places it at a point in the transcoder enable sequence where `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` is already active.

Here is the root cause:
VRR timing registers (TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE) were programmed before TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL was enabled, violating hardware sequencing requirements and causing a hang on ICL. The call to intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings was incorrectly placed in hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder() before the DDI function control is enabled, instead of being done after in the transcoder enable sequence.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder(const struct intel_crtc_state *crtc_state)
 {
 	struct intel_display *display = to_intel_display(crtc_state);
 	struct intel_crtc *crtc = to_intel_crtc(crtc_state->uapi.crtc);
 	enum transcoder cpu_transcoder = crtc_state->cpu_transcoder;
 
 	if (crtc_state->has_pch_encoder) {
 		intel_cpu_transcoder_set_m1_n1(crtc, cpu_transcoder,
 					       &crtc_state->fdi_m_n);
 	} else if (intel_crtc_has_dp_encoder(crtc_state)) {
 		intel_cpu_transcoder_set_m1_n1(crtc, cpu_transcoder,
 					       &crtc_state->dp_m_n);
 		intel_cpu_transcoder_set_m2_n2(crtc, cpu_transcoder,
 					       &crtc_state->dp_m2_n2);
 	}
 
 	intel_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);
-	intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);
 
 	if (cpu_transcoder != TRANSCODER_EDP)
 		intel_de_write(display, TRANS_MULT(display, cpu_transcoder),
 			       crtc_state->pixel_multiplier - 1);
 
 	hsw_set_frame_start_delay(crtc_state);
 
 	hsw_set_transconf(crtc_state);
 }
